title: OurTown Campaign
description: The single input to the campaign kit. Everything the generator renders comes from this record. This is the contract OurTown's app would POST behind the 'Push Your Campaign' button.

id.description: Slug. Used for output directory and zip filename.

headline.description: Campaign-voice headline. Omit to pull from tokens.voice.headlines.

business.description: The HERO. Dominant logo, colors drive the composition.

cause.description: The BENEFICIARY. Secondary logo, colors used as accent only.

image.description: Path or URL. Transparent PNG, 1500px+ on the long edge.

style.description: "cutout" floats a transparent product image with a drop shadow. "photo" frames a photograph that still has its own background inside a rounded card -- which looks deliberate, unlike a bad automatic knockout.

campaignUrl.description: Encoded into the QR and used in all copy assets.

statement.description: One sentence: what the money does. e.g. "Support local youth basketball."

disclosure.description: REQUIRED. Charitable sales promotion / commercial co-venture disclosure, rendered on every asset. Most states that regulate this expect the actual per-unit amount or percentage the nonprofit receives -- not a vague 'supports'. Exact wording is the partners' and their counsel's call; the generator only guarantees it is present and legible.

badges.description: Trust markers. Max 3 -- more reads as clutter at story scale.

moments.description: Which campaign moments to render. Each moment overrides goal.current for its own render.

shortName.description: Used where the full name would not fit, e.g. story format.

logo.description: Path or URL. SVG or transparent PNG.

logoOnDark.description: Optional light-on-dark variant. Falls back to logo.

logoCompact.description: Optional square/badge variant for tight surfaces (sidebar banner, small print). A horizontal lockup shrunk to fit a 300px column becomes unreadable; a compact mark does not. Falls back to logo.

logoStyle.description: "bare" places a transparent mark directly. "tile" is for marks supplied with their own baked-in background (e.g. a badge on a solid brand field) -- it gets rounded corners so the block reads as an intentional badge rather than a rectangle someone forgot to knock out.

colors.description: Partner brand colors. The renderer contrast-corrects these before use -- a pale partner color will be darkened until it is legible rather than shipped unreadable.
